sections.heading: What HEIC Is and Why It Exists
paragraphs: HEIC is the container format that Apple adopted to store photos encoded with the High Efficiency Image Format, which offers roughly half the file size of JPG at comparable quality.
Apple devices capture and store photos this way to stretch storage and iCloud capacity, and live photos and certain depth data ride along in the same container.
The trade-off is compatibility: because the format is newer and patent-encumbered on some platforms, many older systems and web forms simply do not decode it.
Understanding this explains why the same photo that opens instantly on iPhone appears as an unopenable file on a Windows laptop or a standard web form.
